study.title: When I am afraid, I put my trust in You.
study.intro: Thirteen verses come from David's danger among the Philistines at Gath: enemies who twist his words, a refrain of trust that answers fear, tears kept in God's bottle, and a walk in the light of life.
study.context: The heading names David, the tune 'A Dove on Distant Oaks,' and the occasion 'when the Philistines seized him in Gath.' 1 Samuel 21:10–15 records David fleeing Saul to Achish, king of Gath, being recognized as Israel's champion, and pretending madness to escape. Psalm 34's heading recalls the same episode. A refrain of trust appears in verses 3–4 and 10–11: 'In God I trust; I will not be afraid. What can man do to me?' Verse 8's tears in God's bottle and record in His book are images of God's careful attention to suffering. Verse 7's request to 'cast down the nations' is a plea for God's justice against oppressors, not a call to violence by anyone today. The Scripture is loaded unchanged from the bundled BSB, including the heading.
study.peopleNote: The heading names David and the time the Philistines seized him in Gath. His profile includes his flight to Gath and his feigned madness before Achish. The Philistines and Gath are named in the heading; there is no profile for them. Planned paintings show doves, oaks, a tear bottle, a book, and city gates; God is never portrayed as a human body.

verses.title: Men are hounding me
verses.heading: A plea from Gath
verses.meaning: The heading names David, the tune 'A Dove on Distant Oaks,' and the setting: the Philistines seized him in Gath. David cries for mercy because people are hounding him, panting after him like hunters. All day they press their attack. He was surrounded by enemies in a foreign city with no allies. The psalm begins from a place of extreme vulnerability.
verses.context: 1 Samuel 21:10–15 records David fleeing to Achish of Gath, being recognized, and feigning madness to escape. Psalm 34's heading also recalls this event. The tune name may picture a dove far from home.
explore: Be merciful
David asks for grace first. His plea rests on God's mercy, not on his own strength.
Hounding me
The word suggests panting pursuit. His enemies chase him relentlessly.
verses.reflect: Where do you feel pursued or pressed? How could you ask God for mercy there?
verses.alt: A dove perches alone on a distant oak at the edge of a Philistine city.

verses.title: Many proudly assail me
verses.heading: Constant pursuit
verses.meaning: My enemies pursue me all day long, for many proudly assail me. The pursuit is constant and the opponents many. They attack proudly, confident of victory. The repetition of 'all day' from verse 1 shows how exhausting the pressure is. David's situation seems hopeless. Yet the next verse will introduce his central answer.
verses.context: Psalm 3:1 says, 'O LORD, how my foes have increased!' and 1 Samuel 21:11 records the servants of Achish recognizing David as Israel's hero. Psalm 56:2 names a proud multitude against him.
explore: All day long
The pressure is constant. There is no break from the pursuit.
Proudly assail
The enemies are arrogant. They attack from a high position, expecting an easy win.
verses.reflect: When opposition seems large and confident, what keeps you going?
verses.alt: Philistine soldiers with feathered helmets patrol a city gate.

verses.title: When I am afraid
verses.heading: Fear answered by trust
verses.meaning: When I am afraid, I put my trust in You. This short verse is one of the most quoted in the Psalms. David does not say he is never afraid. He admits fear. But fear becomes the moment to trust. The verse does not deny emotion; it shows what to do with it. Trust is a decision made in the presence of fear. David chose it in a foreign city surrounded by enemies.
verses.context: Isaiah 12:2 says, 'I will trust and not be afraid,' and Psalm 27:1 asks, 'Whom shall I fear?' Mark 5:36 records Jesus saying, 'Do not be afraid; just believe.'
explore: When I am afraid
David admits fear. Faith does not mean having no fear at all.
I put my trust
Trust is chosen in fear. It is a response, not a feeling.
verses.reflect: What fear are you facing right now? How could you choose to trust God in it?
verses.alt: A small boat rides steady on a dark sea with a lantern lit at the bow.

verses.title: What can man do?
verses.heading: God's word and fearless trust
verses.meaning: In God, whose word I praise, in God I trust. I will not be afraid. What can man do to me? The refrain develops verse 3. David praises God's word, His promise. Trust leads to fearlessness. The question 'What can man do to me?' is not naive. Humans can do real harm. But they cannot overturn God's purposes. Hebrews 13:6 quotes a similar line from Psalm 118:6.
verses.context: Psalm 118:6 says, 'The LORD is on my side; I will not be afraid. What can man do to me?' and Hebrews 13:6 quotes it. Matthew 10:28 tells disciples not to fear those who kill the body.
explore: Whose word I praise
God's promise is the ground of trust. David praises what God has said.
What can man do?
Humans can harm. They cannot defeat God's purposes.
verses.reflect: What promise of God's word could you hold onto when people frighten you?
verses.alt: An open scroll on a rock is lit by sun amid encircling shadows.

verses.title: They twist my words
verses.heading: Enemies plotting harm
verses.meaning: All day long they twist my words; all their thoughts are on my demise. The enemies distort what David says. They take his words and bend them into accusations. All their thinking aims at harming him. This describes slander and manipulation. In Gath, Achish's servants questioned David's identity (1 Samuel 21:11). The verse names the pain of being misrepresented.
verses.context: Psalm 41:7 describes enemies imagining the worst, and Jeremiah 20:10 says, 'All my trusted friends watch for my fall.' Psalm 56:5 names deliberate distortion.
explore: Twist my words
David's speech is distorted. His enemies misrepresent him.
On my demise
Their thoughts aim at his harm. Their hostility shapes every plan they make.
verses.reflect: Have your words ever been twisted? How could you entrust your reputation to God?
verses.alt: A tangled rope lies knotted beside a scroll with smudged writing.

verses.title: They watch my steps
verses.heading: Lurking conspirators
verses.meaning: They conspire, they lurk, they watch my steps while they wait to take my life. The enemies plan together and hide in wait. They watch every step David takes, hoping for a chance to kill him. The language is of an ambush. David cannot move without being watched. The verse describes the terror of constant surveillance by hostile people.
verses.context: Psalm 10:8–9 describes the wicked lying in wait like a lion, and Luke 20:20 says Jesus' opponents watched Him closely. Psalm 56:6 names conspirators watching David.
explore: They lurk
The enemies hide out of sight. They wait patiently for an opportunity to strike.
Watch my steps
Every move is observed. David cannot escape attention.
verses.reflect: Do you feel watched or scrutinized? How could God's watchfulness over you be a comfort?
verses.alt: Eyes glint from shadows of a doorway along a narrow alley.

verses.title: Will they escape?
verses.heading: A plea for justice
verses.meaning: In spite of such sin, will they escape? In Your anger, O God, cast down the nations. David asks whether his enemies will get away with their evil. He appeals to God's righteous anger to bring down the nations, here meaning the Philistines and other oppressors. This is a prayer for justice, not a call for people to wage war. David leaves the judgment to God.
verses.context: Psalm 7:6 says, 'Arise, O LORD, in Your anger,' and Psalm 9:19 asks God to judge the nations. Romans 12:19 leaves vengeance to God. Psalm 56:7 is a prayer for justice from a fugitive.
explore: Will they escape?
David questions whether evil goes unpunished. He trusts God will act.
Cast down the nations
God's judgment falls on oppressors. David appeals to Him.
verses.reflect: Where do you long for God's justice? How could you leave it in His hands?
verses.alt: A storm cloud gathers over a pagan temple on a hill.

verses.title: Tears in Your bottle
verses.heading: God keeps account
verses.meaning: You have taken account of my wanderings. Put my tears in Your bottle; are they not in Your book? This is one of the tenderest verses in the Psalms. David has been wandering as a fugitive. God has counted every step. David asks God to collect his tears in a bottle, as precious liquid was kept in small skin or clay containers. He knows God records them in His book. No tear is lost or forgotten.
verses.context: Malachi 3:16 speaks of a scroll of remembrance, and Revelation 21:4 promises God will wipe away every tear. Isaiah 25:8 says the Lord GOD will wipe away the tears from all faces.
explore: Taken account of my wanderings
God has counted David's restless steps. Nothing has gone unnoticed.
Your bottle
Tears are kept like something precious. God values them.
verses.reflect: What tears have you shed that you need to know God has kept?
verses.alt: A small glass tear bottle sits on an open book beside a candle.

verses.title: God is on my side
verses.heading: Confidence in God's presence
verses.meaning: Then my enemies will retreat on the day I cry for help. By this I will know that God is on my side. David is sure his enemies will turn back when he calls on God. His confidence is that 'God is for me.' Paul writes, 'If God is for us, who can be against us?' (Romans 8:31). The knowledge of God's support changes everything.
verses.context: Romans 8:31 asks, 'If God is for us, who can be against us?' and Psalm 118:6–7 says, 'The LORD is on my side.' Psalm 56:9 expresses that confidence.
explore: Enemies will retreat
Prayer brings deliverance. On the day David calls, the enemies turn back.
God is on my side
David knows God is for him. That is his greatest assurance.
verses.reflect: How would you live differently if you were sure God is on your side?
verses.alt: Dust trails of retreating chariots fade on a plain at sunrise.

verses.title: Whose word I praise
verses.heading: The refrain expands
verses.meaning: In God, whose word I praise, in the LORD, whose word I praise, the refrain of verse 4 returns, but expanded. David praises God's word twice, once using 'God' and once 'the LORD,' the covenant name. The repetition shows deepening confidence. God's word, His promise, is the ground of trust. This line flows into verse 11. David builds his courage on what God has said.
verses.context: Psalm 119:162 says, 'I rejoice in Your word,' and Isaiah 40:8 says the word of our God stands forever. Psalm 56:10 doubles the praise of verse 4.
explore: God and the LORD
Both names are used. The covenant name makes the praise personal.
Whose word I praise
God's promise is praised. It is the anchor of trust.
verses.reflect: What word or promise from God could you praise out loud today?
verses.alt: A lit oil lamp rests beside an open scroll on a cave ledge.

verses.title: I will not be afraid
verses.heading: Trust repeated
verses.meaning: In God I trust; I will not be afraid. What can man do to me? The refrain is completed exactly as in verse 4. Repetition strengthens the confession. In verse 4, 'flesh' or man is in view; here 'man' appears. Both mean frail humans. The repeated line is meant to be memorized and spoken in moments of fear. David repeats the truth until it steadies him.
verses.context: Psalm 56:4 contains the same words, and Psalm 118:6 echoes them. Philippians 4:6–7 promises God's peace guarding hearts. Psalm 56:11 repeats trust for strength.
explore: Repeated trust
Saying it again strengthens it. Faith grows through repetition.
What can man do?
Humans are frail and mortal. Their power is small beside the God David trusts.
verses.reflect: What sentence of trust could you memorize and repeat when afraid?
verses.alt: A great oak stands firm on a hill as wind bends the grass.

verses.title: Your vows are upon me
verses.heading: Thank offerings promised
verses.meaning: Your vows are upon me, O God; I will render thank offerings to You. David has made promises to God during his trouble. Now he feels bound by them. He will keep them by offering thanksgiving sacrifices. The verse anticipates deliverance and responds with gratitude. Promises made in distress should be kept in relief.
verses.context: Psalm 50:14 says, 'Sacrifice a thank offering to God, and fulfill your vows,' and Ecclesiastes 5:4 says, 'When you make a vow to God, do not delay in fulfilling it.' Psalm 56:12 commits to that.
explore: Vows upon me
David is bound by his promises. He takes them seriously.
Thank offerings
Gratitude is expressed in worship. David will thank God.
verses.reflect: Is there a promise you made to God in a hard time that you need to keep?
verses.alt: A clay jar of oil and loaves are set on an altar with lilies.

verses.title: The light of life
verses.heading: Delivered to walk before God
verses.meaning: For You have delivered my soul from death, and my feet from stumbling, that I may walk before God in the light of life. David gives the reason for thanksgiving. God has rescued him from death and kept him from stumbling. The purpose of deliverance is to walk before God in the light of life. Life is lived in God's presence, guided by His light. The psalm ends in freedom and purpose.
verses.context: Psalm 116:8–9 repeats this almost word for word, and John 8:12 records Jesus saying, 'Whoever follows Me will never walk in the darkness, but will have the light of life.' Psalm 56:13 ends with that walk.
explore: Delivered from death
God saved David's life in Gath. The danger of death has passed.
Light of life
Life is lived in God's presence. His light guides the way.
verses.reflect: What would it mean for you to walk before God in the light of life today?
verses.alt: A sandaled foot steps from a dark gate into bright sunlight on a path.
